question: On 24 small Python tasks, does a small local model that sees the failure message of a failed attempt (arm C) solve more hidden tests than the same model re-sampled from scratch with the same attempt limit (arm B-n)?
hypothesis: Arm C beats arm B-n on hidden-test pass rate by at least the registered margin, because feedback carries information that resampling does not.
falsification: The mean per-task difference (C minus B-n) is below 0.10, or its 95% bootstrap interval includes 0. A tie counts as failure.
limits: The same author wrote the visible and hidden tests, and 24 small tasks says little about real software work.
Local cost is measured as tokens and seconds on one machine; there is no dollar or energy figure.
24 tasks is a small sample: a supported result is a direction, not an established effect.
The model's sampling seed is controlled only if the adapter honours HARNESS_SEED.
stopping_rule: One revision pass to the tasks or prompts after the self-check passes, then lock. No edits after lock; a change means a new experiment directory.
